findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the source of the macOS `sandbox-exec` profile (author it in this ticket with an inline deny-write-outside-worktree ruleset, or embed the profile literally in the skill) and define the scratch-dir path, so the copy-pasteable invocation is self-contained on both platforms.
evidence: AC2: 'Each skill carries a copy-pasteable invocation for both platforms: macOS `sandbox-exec -f <profile>`'
The bwrap counterpart is a self-contained one-liner ('bwrap --ro-bind / / --bind <worktree>'); the sandbox-exec form is not — it depends on an external profile file whose provenance is unstated
AC1 also references 'a scratch dir' as a sandbox-writable location without defining its path/identity
findings.finding: The macOS invocation `sandbox-exec -f <profile>` references a sandbox profile file, but the plan never specifies whether that profile is authored/shipped by this ticket, where it lives, or what deny-write rules it contains — so the 'copy-pasteable invocation' may point at a nonexistent file.
scenarios: An operator copy-pastes the macOS invocation but has no profile file, so the command fails or the agent silently skips the sandbox
findings.suggested_fix: Either embed the sandbox-exec profile body inline in the skill (deny file-write* except worktree + scratch) so it is truly copy-pasteable, or add an AC that the profile file is created and its path is referenced by the invocation.

evidence: AC-2: 'Linux `bwrap --ro-bind / / --bind <worktree>`'

findings.finding: The Linux `bwrap --ro-bind / / --bind <worktree>` invocation the plan ships as a copy-pasteable literal is incomplete at the flag/surface level: it names no `-- COMMAND` to execute under the sandbox, and it omits a writable scratch mount (e.g. `--tmpfs`/`--bind` for a scratch dir) even though AC-1 itself requires 'a scratch dir', plus the usual `--dev`/`--proc` mounts pytest subprocesses need. Repo CI only ever runs `bwrap --version`, so the specific bind-flag surface is UNVERIFIED. An agent pasting this literal verbatim would hit a runtime failure or an under-restricted sandbox.
scenarios: An agent copy-pastes the skill's Linux invocation and the mutation test run either errors (no command / missing /proc) or writes to a scratch path the sandbox never granted

findings.finding: The macOS `sandbox-exec -f <profile>` invocation depends on a profile file whose existence, authorship, and rule content the plan never establishes. `-f <profile>` is a real flag, but `sandbox-exec` is inert without a concrete profile that actually denies writes outside the worktree + scratch dir. findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State in each skill (and assert in the regression test) the mandatory action when no sandbox mechanism is present: do NOT run the mutation unsandboxed — abort and report — rather than falling back to a bare test run.
evidence: ABSENCE: no AC or body text states what the agent does when the sandbox binary is missing or when `shutil.which('bwrap')` is empty on a hardened Linux host

e668 notes bwrap may be absent and "Without `bwrap`, Linux fails closed" — this skill plan carries no equivalent instruction to the agent
findings.finding: The plan instructs agents to run the mutation step inside an OS sandbox but specifies no fallback for the sub-step where neither `sandbox-exec` (macOS) nor `bwrap` (Linux) is available on the host. The agent is left with no defined action — the sibling e668 ticket explicitly fails closed (aborts non-zero, names REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED) for exactly this case, but the skill instruction has no analog, so an agent may silently fall back to the unsandboxed script — the precise path the incident took.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (all bullets) / Why an inline invocation section
scenarios: Agent on a Linux host without bwrap installed reads the skill, finds the mandated command unavailable, and reverts to the ad-hoc `EP.write_text(...)` + `pytest` script with no sandbox — reproducing the incident
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to each skill's sandbox block: "If neither `sandbox-exec` nor `bwrap` is available, do not run the mutation at all — stop and report the missing sandbox; an unsandboxed mutation run is prohibited." Add a test asserting that fail-closed instruction is present in both files.

AC #1 verifies via 'the test asserting both literals are present in both files' — presence of prose, not enforcement of a sandboxed run

scripts/check_destructive_test_exec.py:25-28 frames the layered model explicitly: static/prose controls are 'defence in depth behind the OS sandbox ... never a substitute for it' — the plan does not position the skill prose within this layering

Absence rationale: the plan states no positive rationale for why prose (a control an off-script agent can ignore) is the best available lever, nor that it is a soft layer complementing e668's enforced wrapper
findings.finding: The mechanism is a soft/advisory control whose protection depends entirely on the agent following the added prose, yet the incident's own root cause was an agent going off-script (an ad-hoc /tmp/mut.py that bypassed the sanctioned mutation_gate.py). Adding sandbox prose to the skill does not structurally prevent the identical 'agent writes its own mutation script and skips the sandbox' failure, and the regression test verifies only literal text presence in the file — never that any run is actually sandboxed. The plan does not acknowledge this residual exposure or state why a text-presence assertion is a meaningful control against the very off-script failure mode that caused the incident.
findings.location: Plan sections 'Summary', 'Why an inline invocation, not a dependency on the wrapper', and AC #1/#4

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the sandbox requirement is satisfied (or safely degraded) on Windows and BSD, since the two prescribed invocations cover only macOS and Linux — e.g. a documented platform-detection fallback, an explicit 'refuse to run seeded mutation without a sandbox' rule, or a named-scope limitation.
evidence: "Each skill carries a copy-pasteable invocation for both platforms: macOS `sandbox-exec -f <profile>` and Linux `bwrap --ro-bind / / --bind <worktree>`. Verified by the same test asserting both literals are present in both files."
Support matrix Platform cell includes Windows and BSD alongside macOS and Linux.
`sandbox-exec` is macOS-only; `bwrap`/bubblewrap is Linux-only — neither exists on Windows or BSD by default.
findings.finding: The plan mandates exactly two sandbox invocations — macOS `sandbox-exec -f <profile>` and Linux `bwrap --ro-bind / / --bind <worktree>` — as the required, test-asserted literals, but supplies no invocation for Windows or BSD, both of which are in the supported platform matrix. An agent running the skill on those platforms has neither binary, so the 'run seeded mutation inside an OS sandbox' instruction cannot be followed, and the agent either stalls or falls back to the exact unsandboxed ad-hoc path the plan exists to eliminate.
scenarios: Windows workstation: agent follows rebar-debug's mutation step, has no `sandbox-exec` and no `bwrap`, so the seeded-mutation test run happens unsandboxed — the incident exposure the plan targets is fully present on Windows.
BSD server outside the checkout: `bwrap` is Linux-specific and absent; the agent has no prescribed sandbox and no fallback guidance, so it either blocks or runs hostile mutated code unconstrained.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to each skill a platform-selection rule that (a) picks `sandbox-exec` on macOS, `bwrap` on Linux, and (b) instructs the agent to REFUSE the seeded-mutation run (rather than run it unsandboxed) on any platform lacking a supported sandbox, so Windows/BSD fail closed instead of reintroducing the incident path.
